Unread emails in the inbox are indicated by bold text.
New emails are retrieved by clicking the Get Mail icon and choosing get all new messages.

Clicking the Subject heading sorts the inbox messages by subject.

A slide background refers to all colors and effects applied behind the content of the slide.
Any alteration made to the master slide applies to every slide in the presentation.
The Slide Master view is opened by navigating to View, selecting Master, and clicking Slide Master from the main menu.
The master view toolbar can be used to create, delete, and rename master pages.
A white background can be applied by choosing the blank option under bitmap fill in the Page Setup dialog box.
The text color can be set to black from the Font Effects tab within the Character dialog box.

Gedit text editor comes pre-installed in the Ubuntu Linux operating system.
Gedit can be launched by searching for gedit in Dash Home and clicking the text editor icon.
Gedit can also be launched via the terminal by pressing Ctrl + Alt + T, typing gedit, and pressing Enter.
The default tab name assigned to a new document in gedit is Untitled Document 1.
An asterisk displayed next to a file name in the tab indicates that the file has not been saved.
The status bar displays the cursor position in terms of line number and column number.
The default text mode in gedit is insert mode, indicated as ins.
To save a file, click the File option in the menu bar and select Save.
To close an open file, click File in the menu bar and choose Close.
A new file can be created by clicking the plus sign icon on the toolbar.
An existing document can be opened by clicking File in the menu bar and selecting Open.
Snippets are lines of text or source code frequently used while writing programs.
Snippets is a default plugin in the gedit text editor.
The snippets plugin can be enabled in gedit via Edit, Preferences, checking the snippets box in the plugin tab, and clicking close.
Typing "if" and pressing the Tab key automatically inserts the structure of an if statement.
When an if statement snippet is inserted, the cursor defaults to the condition word.
Auto-closing brackets and quotes is a feature of the intelligent text completion plugin.
Selecting Tools and Manage Snippets from the main menu opens the Manage Snippets dialog box.
Selecting C and clicking its triangle symbol lists all snippets available for C.
The tab trigger for the else if snippet is elif.
Typing "elif" and pressing Tab inserts the syntax for an else if statement.
Clicking the plus icon at the bottom right of the window allows the user to create a new snippet.

Mozilla Thunderbird is a cross-platform email client capable of functioning across different operating systems.
Thunderbird allows users to download email messages from external accounts onto their local computer.
Using POP3 allows users to consolidate accounts into a single inbox inside Thunderbird.
Messages in Thunderbird can be grouped by attributes such as date, sender priority, or custom labels.
Mozilla Thunderbird can be installed on Ubuntu Linux using the Ubuntu Software Center.
In Ubuntu, Thunderbird is opened by typing thunderbird into Dash Home and clicking on the application icon.
Shortcut icons for Get Mail, Write, and Address Book are located beneath the main menu bar in Thunderbird.
The Thunderbird interface contains two panels, with the left panel showing account folders.
In Gmail, POP configuration settings are accessed under the Forwarding and POP/IMAP tab.
Enabling POP in Gmail involves selecting the enable POP option under POP download and saving the changes.
The stdio.h header file defines core input and output functions.
argc shows the total number of command line arguments provided to the program.
argc includes the actual name of the program in its count.
argv stores the actual arguments beginning from index 0.
Index 0 of argv contains the name of the program.
Index 1 of argv contains the first argument passed to the program.

The compilation command entered in the terminal is gcc main-with-args.c -o args.
Executing the program without arguments gives a total count of 1 because the zeroth argument is the executable filename itself.
Passing sunday, monday, and tuesday as arguments produces a total argument count of 4.
To activate change tracking, go to Edit, select Changes, and choose the Record option.
The Show option under Changes must be enabled to visibly record upcoming edits.
Newly inserted text appears in a different color.
Hovering the mouse over inserted text displays the editor's name, insertion date, and time.
The reviewer name attached to edits is determined by the username entered during LibreOffice installation.
Deleting text does not erase it immediately, but flags the line as marked for deletion.
Moving the cursor over deleted text displays the deletion message with reviewer name, date, and time.
LibreOffice Writer displays edits from different reviewers in distinct colors to distinguish their work.
Hovering over edited content in the document confirms whether additions and deletions were made by a specific peer.
A point concerning government institutions developing and promoting FOSS is added at the end of the document.
Print Layout and Web Layout are the two primary view options in LibreOffice Writer.
The Web Layout option displays how the document will appear in a web browser.
Full screen mode is useful for editing documents and displaying them on a projector.
Pressing the Escape key exits Full Screen mode.
A new page break is inserted by choosing Insert, Manual Break, selecting Page Break, and clicking OK.
The Zoom and View Layout dialog box contains the headings Zoom Factor and View Layout.
The 'Fit width and height' option fits the document across the full length and width of the page.
The 100% view displays the page in its actual size.
A custom zoom factor can be entered in the Variable field.
Selecting the Automatic view layout option displays pages side by side.
The controls on the Writer status bar also permit changing the document's view layout and zoom.
The Impress workspace has five tabs known as view buttons.
Notes view enables users to attach notes to each slide that do not show up during the presentation.
Handout view provides the capability to print slides as handouts and select how many slides appear per page.
The Slides pane on the left of the screen shows thumbnails of the presentation slides.
A new blank slide can be added after a selected slide by choosing Insert and then Slide.
A duplicate slide can be created by clicking Insert and then Duplicate Slide.
In Slide Sorter view, a slide can be copied and pasted after the final slide by selecting the After option.
Font family and font size can be adjusted using the text format toolbar.
A dialog box to customize font style and size can be opened by selecting Character under the Format menu.
Font color can be altered by clicking the down arrow situated next to the font color icon.
Text formatting options such as bold, italics, and underline can be applied using toolbar icons.
LibreOffice Impress is equivalent to Microsoft Office PowerPoint.
LibreOffice Impress is free, open-source software available at no cost for use and distribution.
GNU/Linux can be used as the operating system for LibreOffice Impress.
Users should choose the complete option when installing Impress.
The Impress window contains title bars, menu bars, standard bars, formatting bars, and status bars.
A presentation can be initiated from a template by choosing Recommendation of a Strategy.
Slide designs can be selected by choosing Presentation Backgrounds and then Blue Border.
Original can be chosen in the output medium field during presentation setup.
The presenter's name or organization name can be entered in the designated name field.
Impress presentations are saved with the Open Document Format odp extension.
A presentation can be closed by clicking File and then Close.

The lower toolbar includes buttons to enter an element symbol via keyboard and select a new drawing symbol from the periodic table.
Clicking the periodic table button opens the Choose an element window containing a built-in periodic table.
Hovering the cursor over an element like oxygen displays its information inside the info box.
The enter element text box allows users to type an element's symbol directly.
The show implicit hydrogens check box should be deselected in the preferences window if it is checked.
Single bonds to fluorine are initiated by clicking the fluorine button and the single bond button.
A small blue circle appears when placing the cursor over the xenon atom.
Right-clicking on the xenon atom opens its atom popup menu.

The typedef keyword is used to provide symbolic names or aliases to existing or user-defined data types.
The syntax of typedef is typedef existing _ name alias _ name.
An example of typedef is typedef unsigned int uint;.
The palindrome program is compiled using the command gcc pallindrome.c -o pallindrome.
Executing the palindrome program with the input 121 yields the output that the given number is a palindrome number.
A union is a collection of different data types held together.
A union allocates a single, common storage space for all of its members.
Only one member of a union can be accessed at a time.
In union.c, a union named student is declared with the variables english, maths, and science.
A union variable named stud is declared inside the main function.
Running the compiled union program displays the output total is 228.
JChemPaint is a 2D chemical structure editor and viewer.
JChemPaint is a free and open-source cross-platform application developed in Java.
JChemPaint allows importing and exporting structure data in plaintext formats such as SMILES, Molfile, CML, and InChIKeys.
Java must be installed on the system to run JChemPaint.
Java can be installed on Ubuntu using the Synaptic Package Manager.
The downloaded JChemPaint file should be moved from the Downloads folder to the Desktop.
The terminal on Ubuntu can be opened by pressing Ctrl, Alt, and T together.
Typing 'cd desktop' and pressing Enter navigates to the Desktop directory in the terminal.
Running the Java jar command in the terminal launches the JChemPaint window.
JChemPaint can only be opened from the terminal.
On Windows, Java Runtime Environment 7 is installed by accepting the license agreement and choosing the executable installer link.

Emails can be moved from the inbox to the important mails folder via drag and drop.
Clicking search messages under advanced features launches the message search interface.
Search criteria can be set to query messages matching a particular subject term such as ten interesting.
A filter is a rule applied to organise and sort messages within a mailbox.
Selecting manage message filters in advanced features displays the message filters dialog box.
A filter action can be configured to move matching messages to a selected folder.
Clicking run now applies the newly created filter immediately to the mailbox.
Thunderbird configures Gmail accounts automatically, but other email accounts must be configured manually.
POP functionality must be enabled inside the Yahoo account before configuring it in Thunderbird.

Aligning text to the left positions it along the left margin of the document page.
Justify alignment evenly spaces text between the left and right margins of the page.
Bullets and numbering can be accessed through the Format option on the menu bar.
Pressing the Enter key automatically inserts a new bullet point or incremental number.
The Tab and Shift keys are used to increase and decrease indentation levels for bullets.
Bullets and numbering can be disabled by selecting the Numbering Off option.

Storage class specifiers inform the compiler where to store a variable.
The syntax for storage class specifiers consists of the storage specifier, data type, and variable name.
The auto keyword declares an automatic variable that has local scope.
Automatic variables are not initialized automatically and must be initialized explicitly during declaration.
The storage space for auto variables is CPU memory.
Declaring an auto variable globally outside a function produces a file scope declaration error.
An auto variable cannot be initialized globally because it is local to a function.
Static variables are initialized to zero.
Static variables are not destroyed even after program control exits a block.
The value of a static variable is retained across different function calls.
The storage space for static variables is CPU memory.
Notes in Impress serve as additional reference material for the audience or as cues to assist the presenter during a talk.
Clicking on the Notes tab displays a notes text box below the slide for typing notes.
Notes text can be formatted directly using the font type dropdown, font size dropdown, and bullet icon.
To create standard formatting for all notes, open the Notes Master by clicking View, then Master, and selecting Notes Master.
There is a notes master for each master slide utilized in the presentation.
Formatting preferences set on the notes master apply automatically to all notes throughout the presentation.
Text formatting in the notes master can be adjusted by choosing options such as font size 32 and red font color under Character dialog box.
Shapes such as an isosceles triangle can be added from Basic Shapes on the drawing toolbar to act as a logo.
A shape's fill color can be modified via Area in the context menu by selecting Color and choosing Blue 7.
Moving the slide placeholder towards the top of the screen creates more space to resize the notes placeholder.

The Find and Replace feature searches for text and can replace text throughout the document.
Find and Replace can be accessed by clicking the Edit option and then selecting Find and Replace.
Clicking Find All highlights every occurrence of the specified search text across the document.
Clicking Replace All substitutes every instance of the searched text with the replacement text.
The backwards option in Find and Replace searches through text from the bottom upward.
Spellcheck is used to detect spelling errors across the entire document or within a selected portion of text.
Spellcheck checks for spelling errors and provides the option to add an unrecognized word to the user dictionary.
Language configuration is accessed by clicking Tools on the menu bar and selecting Options.
Under the Default languages for documents settings, the Western language field is changed to English USA.
The AutoSpellcheck option must be enabled on the toolbar to utilize spelling and grammar checking.
A newsletter is a publication distributed to subscribers at regular intervals, containing multiple columns to facilitate reading articles.
A new text document can be opened by clicking File, New, and then Text Document.
Columns are added to a document by clicking Format on the menu bar and selecting Columns.
The columns dialog box allows setting the number, width, spacing, and separator line properties of the columns.
Setting the value of the columns field to 2 creates two columns in the text area.
When typing reaches the end of the first column, the cursor automatically advances to the next column.
Pictures can be inserted and resized to properly fit inside a column.
A manual column break is inserted by clicking Insert, selecting Manual Break, choosing Column break, and clicking OK.
Selecting Green 4 from the background color icon changes the background of selected text to light green.
Banners can be added to the document by selecting the Text option from the Drawing toolbar and placing a text box.
Text animation options can be accessed by right-clicking the text and selecting Text from the context menu.
Selecting the Blink effect from the Text Animation tab causes the text to flash.
Presentations cannot be edited while in slide show mode.
The F5 function key can be used to start a slide show.
Pressing the escape button exits the slide show.
The mouse pointer as pen option allows users to draw and write on the presentation during slide show mode.
Pressing the space bar advances the presentation to the next slide.
Slide transitions are visual effects applied when moving from one slide to another in a presentation.
Clicking on the Slide Sorter tab displays all slides in the presentation.
Slides can be rearranged by dragging and dropping a selected slide to a new position.
Transitions can be applied to slides by selecting slide transitions in the task pane.
Transition speed can be adjusted by selecting an option from the speed dropdown menu.

JChemPaint preferences can be accessed through the Edit menu.

The Look and Feel section dropdown includes options for System, Metal, Nimbus, Motif, GTK, and Windows.
